items.rationale: The washing-machine escape falls under §2.4.2. Section 7.1.7(h) covers necessary residue removal from the wetted floor; €65 allows for a localized clean.
Section 7.1.7(h) covers cleaning the documented wetted hallway floor, not general housekeeping. €80 allows for the affected area only.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers checking the source and confirming that it no longer leaks, even if the appliance itself is uninsured. €85 allows for a short on-site inspection without appliance repair.

items.description: Remove and dispose of damaged skirting
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.7(a) and 5.2.1 cover removing and disposing of the affected skirting. €95 allows for localized removal and a small amount of waste.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.9 limit payment to replacing the affected runs at the pre-loss standard. €240 allows for standard skirting, fixings and fitting.

items.description: Clean and repaint unaffected upstairs bedroom
items.rationale: Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude work in a separate room with no established damage.

items.description: Measure moisture in utility-room and hallway floors
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(b) covers moisture measurement in both affected rooms. €165 follows the comparable floor and wall-base measurement in Case 21.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary drying of the affected floor areas. €100 allows for drying work distinct from the separately billed rental and labour; §7.1.8(c) bars overlap.
Section 7.1.7(e) expressly covers equipment hire for necessary drying. €55 allows for modest rental, provided it is not already included in the drying charge under §7.1.8(c).

Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary trade labour at customary rates. Four hours at about €47 gross gives €188 if the time is attributable to the affected rooms and not already billed elsewhere under §7.1.8(c).
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) do not extend drying or related measurement to a separate room with no documented damage.

Section 5.2.6 covers specialist transport but gives restoration first call on the €1,190 gross per-item cap (€1,000 plus 19% VAT). If restoration leaves a balance, transport is first in invoice order and an ordinary one-way charge is about €95.
Section 5.2.6 covers qualified assessment only from the balance left after restoration and the earlier transport charge. If a balance remains, about €120 is a reasonable capped contribution.
Section 5.2.6 covers drying and stabilisation, but this line receives only what remains of the €1,190 gross cap after restoration, transport and assessment. A positive residual is estimated at €100.

The affected painting was professionally assessed and is not individually scheduled, so §5.2.6 applies a €1,000 net cap and allocates it to restoration first. Full specialist restoration is expected to absorb the cap: €1,000 × 1.19 = €1,190 gross with incurred VAT under §7.7.
Section 5.2.6 requires the item itself to have been affected by the insured event. The second painting was unaffected and remains excluded as contents under §4.3(d).
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes separately billed administrative and processing charges. The fee is also not a conservation measure listed in §5.2.6.
